### 3.3.4 Doctrinal Construction of Law and the Reconstruction of Individual Sovereignty

Faced with the reality that choice architectures within AI prompts and autonomous systems are capable of unconsciously influencing, steering, and even hijacking human decision-making, traditional positive legal systems appear bewildered and lagging behind (Calo, 2014). Classical Civil Law doctrines, as stipulated in Articles 1320 through 1328 of the Indonesian Civil Code (*Burgerlijk Wetboek*), rest upon the 19th-century liberal philosophical assumption that a contract or legal act arises from the free will
